job.title: Developer-in-Residence
job.description:
**Overview**

**Organization:** napari (a NumFOCUS Sponsored Project)  
**Position Type:** Independent contractor agreement. Global, 100% Remote.  
**Duration:** One year, possibility to extend.  
**Commitment:** 0.4 to 1.0 FTE (Full-Time Equivalent, 35 hrs/week, 48-weeks) /
Minimum 0.4 FTE  
**Compensation:** USD \$59.50 per hour. $100k/yr at 1.0 FTE.  
**Benefits:** Paid travel to conferences, workshops, and hackathons. Fully
flexible work hours. As an independent contractor position, traditional employee
benefits such as health insurance and PTO are not provided; contractor will bill
hourly for hours worked in the prior month.  
**Target Start Date:** Preferred November or December 2026. Open to January 2027
and later.

**About napari**

[napari](https://napari.org/) is a fast, interactive, multi-dimensional data
viewer for Python. As a healthy and growing open-source project, napari relies
on a dedicated community to drive its development and maintain its ecosystem of
core libraries and plugins. There is a particular need for attention to the
napari [core library](https://github.com/napari/napari) to address outstanding
architectural issues and create a well-constructed core that will make project
maintenance easier and enable new viewer features.

**The Role**

We are seeking **Remote Developers-in-Residence (DiR)** to work on napari
repositories to meet strategic roadmap priorities and maintain the health of the
project.

You will work with the current Developers-in-Residence, core team members, and
community to plan and deliver key items on the napari Roadmap, with a particular
focus on the User-facing Improvements items in the
[Core Library](https://napari.org/stable/roadmaps/active_roadmap.html#core-library)
section.

We work fully remotely with no set working hours, since there’s no
headquarters\! What matters more is how you stay connected: attending community
meetings, communicating your progress and blockers on
[Zulip](https://napari.zulipchat.com/), and keeping PRs updated and legible to
others. Success in this role means being comfortable working autonomously,
reaching out for help when you need it, and making your work visible and
coordinated with the wider team.

You will serve as a core technical anchor to address architectural challenges,
accelerate review cycles, and mentor community developers. You will be guided by
the napari Steering Council and members of the napari core team. This is a
unique opportunity to shape the future of a widely used scientific visualization
tool and to meet the needs of a growing and diverse community of developers and
users.

**Selection Criteria**

Qualified candidates should have intermediate to advanced experience developing
software with the Python programming language, version control with Git,
familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, and writing and maintaining tests. Ideal
candidates may demonstrate one or more of the following:

1. Contribution to and maintenance of Open Source Software.  
2. Use of and contribution to napari and/or its plugin ecosystem.
3. Experience in computer science and software engineering fundamentals,
  including algorithms and data structures, performance, and architecture
  design patterns.  
4. Training in medical imaging, bioimaging, geosciences, physics, and other
  image data-adjacent fields.  
5. Experience with Qt, graphics programming, and/or image rendering.

**Key Responsibilities**

Your time will be distributed across three core focus areas:

1. Feature Development & Architecture (~60%)

- **Strategic Roadmap Execution:** Design, build and refactor core features in
  alignment with the
  [napari Roadmap](https://napari.org/stable/roadmaps/active_roadmap.html).  
- **Core Modularization:** Untangle legacy components to build a lightweight,
  fast, and modular core viewer that simplifies future maintenance and supports
  alternative rendering backends.  
- **Ecosystem Collaboration** Contribute features, bug-fixes, and PR reviews to
  napari-adjacent repositories (e.g., `vispy`, `pyapp-kit` suite).  
- **Documentation:** Write and maintain clear technical specifications, design
  documents, and user references alongside development and maintenance work.

2. Project Maintenance (~20%)

- **Triage:** Provide empathetic, constructive, and timely review on pull
  requests and issues in the napari organization repositories, address the PR
  and issue backlog, and keep the project moving forward.
- **Developer Experience & Tooling:** Implement ways to make the project easier
  to work with (e.g., improving tests, CI workflows, style consistency,
  automation).
- **Release Readiness:** Assist with release stabilization, testing release
  candidates, and resolving pre-release blockers.

3. Community Enablement & Outreach (~20%)

- **Community Discussions & Meetings:** Participate actively in community
  developer meetings, architecture discussions, and technical Zulip chat
  threads.
- **Technical Mentorship:** Onboard and mentor community contributors to the
  napari project.
- **Conferences & Technical Outreach:** Prepare proposals, author technical
  materials, and present talks or tutorials representing napari at open-source
  and scientific conferences (e.g., SciPy, EuroSciPy), workshops, and
  hackathons.

**How to Apply**

To apply, please submit the following to
[the application typeform](https://napari.typeform.com/2026-job-search):

1. Your resume or CV.
2. A link to your GitHub profile or other software portfolio highlighting
  representative software development. Highlight, if applicable, napari-related
  work.
3. A statement of interest (1 page) describing your experience with Python
  development, your connection to or interest in napari, and what you would
  like to engage with in the DiR role.
4. Representative contribution (½ page): PR, issue discussion, etc — briefly
  explain what problem you solved and your approach. Please provide a link to
  the contribution.
5. Availability and Commitment: Please specify your preferred weekly hours/FTE
  commitment and start date availability and preference.
6. Interview Availability: What availability (dates and times) do you have for
  interviews, starting October 7th? Please include a timezone.
7. Contractor Status: I confirm that I understand this is an independent
  contractor position (not an employee role), and that I have looked into what
  this means for me legally and financially in my country/region — including
  tax obligations, invoicing, and any registration requirements — before
  applying. Please reach out with any questions.

**Interview Selection Process**

Candidate applications will be scored on a rubric evaluating Python and software
engineering; open source and community work; domain and technical context; and
communication and interest. Selected applicants will receive a request to
schedule a 60-minute online interview with two napari team members. Thirty-six
hours prior to the interview, the applicant will receive a link to a demo
repository and be asked to review a toy pull request, to be returned at least
twelve hours prior to the interview. All candidates will be contacted with the
outcome of their application as early as practicable.
